input.question: What does a photon decay into?
input.ground_truth: There are limits on the photon mass meaning there are experimentally allowed very small values. Some theories allow a small photon mass but according to the Standard Model the photon is massless. If correct this means it will never decay and the electromagnetic force range is infinite. When a high energy photon interacts with matter it can be converted into an electron positron pair, but if the photon has finite mass this couldn't be a possible decay mode. Having mass means the photon has a rest frame. In that rest frame, energy and momentum need to be conserved just as it does in any frame. The decay products can't add up to more than the mass of the photon, leaving only electron neutrino - antineutrino pair or some undiscovered light elementary particles.
